statement.p: Use Lagrange multipliers to find the maximum and minimum values of f(x,y) = x - 3 y subject to the constraint x^2 + 2 y^2 = 22, if such values exist.

p.em: (For either value, enter DNE if there is no such value.)

static.solution: f(x,y)= x - 3 y and our equation of constraint is g(x,y) = x^2 + 2 y^2 = 22. To optimize f(x,y) with Lagrange multipliers we solve the following system of equations f_{x}(x,y) = \lambda g_{x}(x,y),\qquad\mbox{so } 1 = 2\lambda x, f_{y}(x,y) = \lambda g_{y}(x,y),\qquad\mbox{so } -3 = 4\lambda y, and g(x,y) = 22,\qquad\mbox{so } x^2 + 2 y^2 = 22. Solving for \lambda gives us \lambda = \frac{1}{2 x} = \frac{-3}{4 y}, which we can use to find x in terms of y: x = -\frac{2}{3}\,y. Using this relation in our equation of constraint, we can solve for y: x^2 + 2 y^2 = 22, so (-\frac{2}{3}\, y)^2 + 2 y^2 = 22, and thus ((\frac{2}{3})^2 + 2)\, y^2 = 22. So, solving for y, we have y = \pm 3, and x = \mp 2. Thus, the critical points are (-2,3) and (2,-3). Since the constraint is closed and bounded, maximum and minimum values of f subject to the constraint exist. Evaluating f at the critical points, we find that the maximum value is f(2,-3) = (2) + 3(3) = 11 and the minimum value is f(-2,3) = -(2) - 3(3) = -11.
